subject: Twilight needs a loving home
content:
Good morning

I am reaching out for my daughters kitten Twilight. She is less than 1yr
old she has been spayed, she is very calm, sweet and very much loved.

Unfortunately due to my daughter and her husbands busy schedule(s) they are
unable to accommodate Twilight with the time she needs. Love and affection
was never an issue but the pair of them are hardly even home.

Now with both of their jobs are being relocated they have to move into a
place that has a Strict no pet policy. I myself cannot have pets due to
terrible allergies and even with that I’d take her in if my own apartment
didn’t have a no pet policy as well.

If there is any way you could help out and take her in find her a loving
home that can spend time with her or refer us to another agency or place we
would be eternally greatful.


Please let us know as soon as your able as we have no other options. A few
shelters we visited have said they would put her down and that would not be
good for my daughters conscious or mental well being knowing that
Twilight’s fate would be decided in that way due to her career
progressions.

We look forward to speaking with you and or seeing you soon. Thank you soo
much for your time.

I've also attached pictures below if you need help getting started but totally up to you if you want to change it up.

As for the deadline...I plan on having this post come out in November 8th. subject: Advice on outside cat rehoming.
content:
Hi! I'm very sorry to reach out to this organization like this as I know
this email is most likely used for better purposes, but I am having a
problem of my own that I feel like only some kitty cat experts could help
me with. To try to keep it short and simple, there is a cat in my
possession that I need to rehome, but due to special circumstances, I have
no idea how. About a year and a half ago I found a stray cat living in my
attic of a home I used to share with 4 different roommates. Over the course
of 6 months she won my heart over, and I started taking complete care of
her (vet visits, vaccines, spaying, and feeding twice a day.) At this time
she was an outdoor/indoor cat, and she was living the dream. Eventually
however, we ended up needing to move out of that place and go our
separate ways. I felt that it was necessary to take her in completely as
she had developed a dependence on me, and so I did this, on the terms of
her becoming an inside cat. Over the course of the next year I had tried
everything in my power to get her accustomed to it. I tried catios, wall
shelves, making a playground in my house, scheduled playtimes, leash
training, walks outside daily, training, etc... None of it ever worked.
Eventually I broke and let her outside on an indoor/outdoor basis again,
and she has never been happier. While this may seem like a great thing,
it's not really. First and foremost, the area I live in here at UTA is
surrounded by 4 major busy streets. She has ample room behind us, but if
she were to go anywhere else it could mean danger for her. While this part
is still sort of working out regardless of these facts, the main problem is
that I have no idea how long I can afford to be in this house with a
backyard for her to roam in. With my gradually decreasing budget, loan
expenses, and so on, I do not think I can keep this house or any house with
a yard like this for much longer. In conclusion, it has come to my
attention that she might be better off in a different home. The caveat here
is that I have no idea how to do that. She is an extremely friendly cat,
but only to people. She hates cats, and other animals are tolerable*. She
thrives on being outdoors, but she also loves to come in constantly to
socialize and to be a huge cuddlebug. She doesn't fit into one category.
She would do terribly in a shelter because of other cats, and she's not
just a barn cat that only wants to be outside. I have no idea where to put
her. If y'all managed to read any of this, is there any insight I can
recieve on this situation? I love this girl to death, and I really need to
find a place that's fitting for her.

Hey friends,

I met SpaceMachine (James) twenty years ago in a wild New York kitchen, two artists trapped in day jobs, dreaming of sound and cinema. Life sent us both down rough roads: addiction, loss, broken dreams. But art, and friendship, became our way back.

Years later, James was hit by a car, died, and was revived. His wife disappeared with their son. Still, he refused to quit. He found a new partner in drummer Eric Blitz, a musician living with a disability who defies every limit behind his drums. Together, they rebuilt SpaceMachine from the ashes.

When my own film project collapsed, I turned my camera toward James. What started as documenting his studio sessions became something more, a raw, moving documentary about survival, brotherhood, and the healing power of music. Watching James pour his pain into melody reminded me: Love and hope still exist, even in chaos.
